claim_verdicts.source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/app-pg-isready.html (Exit Status); reviewer run, throwaway container rv-pgtest, postgres:17.6-alpine, 2026-09-26
claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs: "pg_isready returns 0 to the shell if the server is accepting connections normally" — first half holds. Second half fails as a guarantee: with a 12 s init script, in-container `pg_isready` printed "/var/run/postgresql:5432 - accepting connections" from second 2 while the log showed "running /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/s.sql"; "PostgreSQL init process complete" came ~12 s later. The healthcheck can pass while schema.sql/seed.sql still run.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: pg_isready succeeds when the server is accepting connections; after the db container starts, Postgres needs a few seconds before that happens.

issues.quote: That command succeeds only when Postgres accepts connections for that user and database.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and wrong. PostgreSQL 17 pg_isready Notes: "It is not necessary to supply correct user name, password, or database name values to obtain the server status". Exit 0 means the server is accepting connections at all; `-U donhang -d donhang` does not make it check that user or database.
issues.fix: Replace with: "That command succeeds when the Postgres server accepts connections." If the writer wants to explain -U/-d, add only: "`-U` and `-d` are what it logs in as; the check does not depend on them." Add the sentence to claims with version_key postgresql.

issues.quote: and on the very first start even longer, while it runs `schema.sql` and `seed.sql`.
issues.text: Next to "With `condition: service_healthy`, Compose waits until the `db` healthcheck succeeds", this implies the wait covers the init scripts. It does not: the image runs them on a temporary server that in-container pg_isready (Unix socket) already reports as "accepting connections" (reviewer run, claim 4). On a first start the healthcheck can pass before schema.sql/seed.sql finish.
issues.fix: Delete the clause ", and on the very first start even longer, while it runs `schema.sql` and `seed.sql`" so the sentence ends at "before it accepts connections." Update claim 4 to the suggested_text. Do not add the init-race detail; it is beyond this lesson.

issues.text: Key a and its explanation ("succeeds only when the server is accepting connections for that user and database") repeat the wrong pg_isready claim. The key is only the least-wrong option: pg_isready tests whether the server accepts connections, not whether it does so for `donhang`.
issues.fix: Option a (en): "Whether the Postgres server accepts connections"; vi: "Server Postgres có nhận kết nối không". Explanation correct (en): "`pg_isready` succeeds when the Postgres server is accepting connections."; vi: "`pg_isready` thành công khi server Postgres đang nhận kết nối."

issues.quote: `localhost:5432` works from your laptop only because the lab publishes that port there … makes the API fail at startup with a connection refused error.
issues.text: Unlisted claim. Both parts are true (docker-compose.yml@stage-1 L70-71 `"5432:5432"`; reviewer run of donhang-api:stage-1 with Host=localhost -> "Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1:5432 ---> SocketException (111): Connection refused"), but they are not in the ledger.
issues.fix: Add a claim (kind behavior, section 6, version_key docker): "The db service publishes 5432:5432, so localhost:5432 reaches Postgres from the host; in the api container, Host=localhost fails at startup with Npgsql 'Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1:5432' / 'Connection refused'." Source: this review's run. No text change.

issues.quote: healthcheck — a command Docker runs inside a container every few seconds
issues.text: The interval is whatever the healthcheck sets; Docker's default `--interval` is `30s` (Dockerfile reference, HEALTHCHECK options). "Every few seconds" holds for this lab's `interval: 3s`, not as a definition.
issues.fix: Change to: "healthcheck — a command Docker runs inside a container at a set interval (every 3 seconds in the lab); after it succeeds, the container counts as healthy."

issues.quote: `build` tells Compose to build the image from `DonHang.Api/Dockerfile`
issues.text: With both `build` and `image` and no `pull_policy`, Compose "attempts to pull the image first and then builds from source if the image isn't found in the registry or platform cache" (compose-file/build.md L26-28). In the reviewer's `docker compose up -d api` nothing was built, because donhang-api:stage-1 already existed.
issues.fix: Change to: "`build` tells Compose how to build the image from `DonHang.Api/Dockerfile` when it doesn't have `donhang-api:stage-1` yet, with the repository root as ..." Keep the rest of the sentence.
